samples.text:
Today we have many machines and devices which make our daily tasks faster, for example washing machines, dishwashers and online shopping. However, many people say that they have less free time than before. This essay will explain why this happens and what can be done about it.

There are some reasons for this problem. The main reason is that technology makes people work more. Because of smartphones and emails, people can be contacted by their boss in any time, even in the evening or at the weekend, so work never finish. Secondly, people spend a lot of their free time on social media and watching videos, and they do not notice how many hours they lose. For example, someone may plan to check their phone for five minutes but then scroll for one hour. Also, life today is more competitive, so people try to do more activities, such as taking extra courses or working second job, to earn more money.

There are several things that can help people to have more free time. Firstly, companies should make rules that employees do not have to answer emails after working hours. Secondly, people should control how much time they spend on their phones, for example by turning off notifications or using apps which limits screen time. Finally, people should learn to say no to some activities and choose what is really important for them.

In conclusion, people feel they have less free time because technology connects them to work all the time and because they waste time on their phones. I think both employers and individuals needs to make changes to solve this problem.
samples.why: Both questions answered with relevant, practical points · solutions briefly developed · mechanical linking (Firstly, Secondly, Finally) · adequate everyday vocabulary · errors in prepositions, articles and agreement that do not affect understanding.

samples.text:
Modern technology has dramatically reduced the time needed for many routine tasks, from washing clothes to paying bills. Paradoxically, however, many people complain that they have less leisure time than ever. This essay will explain the reasons for this contradiction and suggest ways of addressing it.

One important reason is that the time saved by technology is often filled with more work. Laptops and smartphones mean that employees can be reached at any hour, and many feel obliged to reply to messages in the evening or at weekends, so the boundary between work and home life has become blurred. In addition, expectations have risen along with efficiency. Because tasks can be completed more quickly, employers and individuals simply try to do more of them, and people end up busier rather than more relaxed. Technology also consumes free time directly. Social media and streaming services are designed to hold users' attention, and hours spent scrolling often feel neither restful nor satisfying, which increases the impression that there is never enough time.

Several measures could help to address this situation. At the workplace level, companies could introduce clear policies limiting contact outside working hours, and governments could consider a legal right to disconnect. More flexible working arrangements, such as compressed working weeks, might also give employees longer periods of genuine rest. On a personal level, individuals can take control of their digital habits by disabling non-essential notifications, setting limits on app usage and keeping certain times of the day free from screens. Finally, people may benefit from prioritising fewer activities rather than trying to fill every moment productively.

In conclusion, people have less free time despite technological progress because work has expanded into their personal lives, expectations have risen and digital entertainment absorb many hours. Workplace policies and more mindful use of technology could help them regain valuable leisure time.
samples.why: Both parts answered clearly with extended reasoning · good paragraph organisation and a range of cohesive devices · appropriate collocations (right to disconnect, blurred boundary) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Technology has spared people countless hours of domestic drudgery and administrative effort, yet complaints about a lack of time have never been more common. This apparent contradiction can be explained by the way the time saved is reabsorbed by work and digital distraction, and reclaiming leisure will require action from employers, governments and individuals alike.

The first explanation lies in the erosion of boundaries between work and private life. Devices that make it possible to work from anywhere also make it possible to be contacted everywhere, and in many workplaces an unspoken expectation has developed that emails will be answered promptly, whatever the hour. As a result, even time spent at home is frequently interrupted by professional demands. Secondly, efficiency tends to raise expectations rather than reduce effort: when a task can be completed in half the time, the typical response is to take on more tasks, not to rest. Finally, much of the time technology frees is quietly consumed by technology itself. Social media feeds and streaming platforms are deliberately designed to be absorbing, and hours spent on them rarely feel like genuine leisure, leaving people both occupied and unrefreshed.

Addressing the problem requires structural as well as personal change. Employers could make it clear that staff are not required to respond outside working hours, and legislation guaranteeing a right to disconnect would give such policies greater force. Shorter working weeks, where output can be maintained, would allow productivity gains to be shared with workers as additional free time rather than extra workload. Individuals, too, can reclaim hours by curbing their use of attention-grabbing apps, disabling notifications and deliberately protecting periods of the day for rest, hobbies or social contact.

In conclusion, people feel short of time because technology has extended the reach of work, raised expectations and created new distractions. Firmer boundaries set by employers and governments, combined with more deliberate personal habits, would allow the time saved by technology to become genuine free time.
samples.why: Both questions answered fully with a well-reasoned explanation of the paradox · ideas logically sequenced and developed · wide, precise vocabulary (drudgery, reabsorbed, curbing) · wide range of accurate structures.
